cues.en: I'm on the phone with Jim on one of our regular check ins. Jim, it's just nothing's happening.
cues.zh: 我正在和Jim通电话，这是我们例行沟通的其中一次。Jim，就是啥动静都没有。

cues.en: Hey, Jim.
cues.zh: 嘿，Jim。

cues.en: It's going well. We We had some serious bouts of wind.
cues.zh: 进展挺顺利的。我们……我们这儿刮了几场大风。

cues.en: But other than that, things are fairly well set up here. We've got some continuous time lapse going. It's starting, Adam. I think Adam is starting.
cues.zh: 但除此之外，这边一切安排得挺妥当。我们一直在连续拍延时。开始了，Adam。我想Adam要开始了。

cues.en: Oh, wait, Jim. Jim. This is... The the big piece is starting to cast. Let me call you back. Call him back.
cues.zh: 哦，等等，Jim。Jim。这是……那那大件的东西开始浇铸了。我回头再打给你。回头再打给他。

cues.en: Okay. Bye.
cues.zh: 好。再见。

cues.en: It's still going? Yeah. In that v section right there.
cues.zh: 还在放？对。就在那个 V 形区域。

cues.en: Holy shit. Look at that big bird rolling.
cues.zh: 我靠。看那只大鸟在翻滚。

cues.en: All four run. Right? Yeah. Look at that.
cues.zh: 四个都跑起来了。对吧？对。看那个。

cues.en: You see how... Look look at the whole thing.
cues.zh: 你看这……看，看整个东西。

cues.en: The calving face is 300, sometimes 400 feet tall.
cues.zh: 崩解面有 300 英尺高，有时 400 英尺。

cues.en: Pieces of ice were shooting up out of the ocean 600 feet and then falling.
cues.zh: 冰块从海里冲到 600 英尺高，然后又落下来。

cues.en: Only way that you can really try to put it into scale with human references is if you imagine Manhattan.
cues.zh: 真要拿人的参照物来想象它的规模，只能想象曼哈顿。

cues.en: And all of a sudden,
cues.zh: 突然之间，

cues.en: all of those buildings just start to rumble and quake and peel off and just fall over and fall over and roll around.
cues.zh: 所有这些建筑开始轰隆震动、剥落，然后倒下、倒下、翻滚。

cues.en: This whole massive city
cues.zh: 整座巨大的城市

cues.en: just breaking
cues.zh: 就这样崩裂

cues.en: apart in front of your eyes.
cues.zh: 在你眼前四分五裂。

cues.en: We're just observers.
cues.zh: 我们只是观察者。

cues.en: These two little dots on the side of the mouth.
cues.zh: 在入海口一侧的那两个小点。

cues.en: And we watched and recorded
cues.zh: 我们观察并记录下了

cues.en: the largest witness cabin event ever caught on tape.
cues.zh: 有录像记录以来最大的冰崩事件。

cues.en: So how big was this calving event that we just looked at? We'll resort to some illustrations again to give you a sense of scale.
cues.zh: 那么我们刚才看到的这次冰崩事件有多大？我们再借助一些示意图，让你感受一下规模。

cues.en: It's as if the entire lower tip of Manhattan broke off,
cues.zh: 就好像曼哈顿最南端整个断裂脱落了一样，

cues.en: except that the thickness, the height of it is equivalent to buildings that are two and a half or three times higher than they are.
cues.zh: 只不过它的厚度——也就是高度——相当于那些建筑高度的两倍半到三倍。

cues.en: That's a magical,
cues.zh: 这真是神奇，

cues.en: miraculous,
cues.zh: 不可思议，

cues.en: horrible,
cues.zh: 恐怖，

cues.en: scary thing.
cues.zh: 吓人的事情。

cues.en: I don't know that anybody's really seen the miracle and horror of that.
cues.zh: 我不确定有没有人真正见识过其中的神奇与恐怖。

cues.en: It took a hundred years for it to retreat eight miles from 1900 to 2000.
cues.zh: 从1900年到2000年，它用了一百年才后退八英里。

cues.en: From 2000
to 2010, it retreated nine miles. So in ten years, it retreated more than it had in the previous one hundred.
cues.zh: 到2010年，它后退了九英里。所以十年间，它后退的距离比之前一百年还多。
